name: Mashlink – Internal Linking for SEO
author: Sikander Jafar

sections.description:
Mashlink, built by WPmash, is a free, lightweight internal linking plugin that finds orphan pages, fixes weak links and builds new ones with a smart suggestion system.

Flag too much anchor text use, find broken links and spot internal links that still point to redirected pages.

Get link opportunities in the block editor and insert a link in one click. Works with custom post types, ACF fields and ACF blocks.

Tested and maintained by an experienced SEO strategist using it on real websites with thousands of pages to improve their internal linking.

Find internal linking opportunities with a smart system

  • Suggestions appear in the block editor sidebar, each one shown in context.
  • Insert the link in one click. The editor scrolls to it.
  • Pages you already link to are never suggested again.
  • Works with ACF WYSIWYG fields and ACF blocks.
  • Semantic matching: related words such as “cost” and “price” count as the same meaning, so a page about “roof repair cost” is also suggested for the text “price to fix a roof”. A short built-in list is used, and the Pro add-on lets you add your own large list.
  • Also matches the focus keyphrases saved by Yoast SEO, Rank Math, SEOPress and All in One SEO, and the SEO title saved by Slim SEO.

Link report

  • Number of internal links in and out for every published post, page and custom post type.
  • Colour tags for isolated content, content with no incoming links, dead ends (no outgoing links) and connected content.
  • Overall Link Health score with a summary of the issues found.
  • Depth column that shows how many clicks each page is from the homepage.
  • Sortable columns, search by title or URL, and a post type filter.
  • Click a number under Incoming links or Outgoing links to see every link with its anchor text, then use Edit link (opens the editor with the link highlighted) or Remove link.

Anchor text tracking

  • Every anchor text with the number of times it is used and the pages that use it.
  • An anchor is flagged in red as overused only when the same anchor links to one page more than 4 times AND makes up more than 15% of the links to that page. Anchors spread across many pages (like “read more”) are not flagged. Both numbers can be changed with the wpmash_ila_anchor_limit and wpmash_ila_anchor_share filters.
  • An Ignore button for anchors that are fine to repeat.

Deep scan

  • Reads the rendered page, so links added by templates, theme builders, page builders and query loops are counted.
  • Reads synced patterns and HTML stored in custom fields such as ACF.

Broken and redirected links

  • Requests each internal link from your site and reports errors, redirects, redirect chains and redirect loops.
  • Shows the link as written, the URL it should point to, the anchor text and every page that contains it, with an Edit link.

Optional add-on: Mashlink Pro

Mashlink Pro – Add-on is a separate paid plugin sold on mashlinkwp.com. Everything in this plugin stays free. Pro adds:

  • Fix tab: fixes isolated, no-incoming and dead-end pages in bulk, with reviewed proposals and one-click undo.
  • Related words: large semantic related-word lists for your niche, built with an AI assistant.
  • Topical Clusters map: an interactive map of your pillar pages and topic clusters.
  • Report: print or save a link report, with your own branding, or e-mail it on a schedule with a CSV.
  • AI access: a read-only connection that lets Claude read your link data.

Extras

  • CSV export of any tab, with the current filters applied.
  • A Diagnose box that shows what the scan sees on a single page.
  • Pages are rescanned automatically when saved.
  • No custom database tables and no front-end output.

Compatibility

Tested with:

  • WordPress 7.1.5 and PHP 8.4.
  • Block editor (Gutenberg).
  • Block themes and themes by GeneratePress, with GenerateBlocks.

Supported (the scan reads the rendered page, but these have not been tested yet):

  • Block themes and themes such as Kadence, Astra and the default WordPress themes.
  • Page builders such as Elementor, Breakdance and Bricks. Mashlink detects them and counts the links they output.
  • Custom post types, ACF fields and ACF blocks.

Test on a staging copy and keep a backup before installing on a live site.

Privacy

The plugin sends no data to third parties and loads no external code. It reads the focus keyphrases that SEO plugins save in your own database to improve link suggestions; nothing is sent anywhere. The deep scan and the link check request your own site’s URLs from your server, and only administrators can start them. When a link redirects to another website, the plugin reports the destination and does not request it.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install the zip from Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Open Tools > Mashlink (or click Settings on the Plugins screen) and click Run full scan.
  4. Open the Broken & redirected links tab and click Check links.
sections.faq:
Does the plugin change my content?

Only when you ask it to. Scanning reads posts and stores the results in its own post meta. A page changes only when you click Remove link in the report or Insert link in the editor panel, and WordPress keeps a revision.

Does it slow down my site?

The plugin adds nothing to the pages visitors see. Scans run in the admin in small batches, and a deep scan requests each page from your own site, which is why it takes longer.

Why does a page show no links?

The links may come from a template or a dynamic field. Run a deep scan, or enter the page’s ID or URL in the Diagnose box to see what the scan found and which part of the page it read. Some hosts and firewalls block a site from requesting its own pages, and the Diagnose box shows the HTTP response in that case.

Why are some links missing from the report?

The report counts body text links only. Navigation, categories, buttons, query loops and links without text are skipped by design. The “Include button links” checkbox adds button links.

Does it check external links?

No. The link checker covers links to your own site, and a redirect that leaves the site is reported with its destination.

How are anchors compared?

Anchor text is compared across the whole site without regard to capital letters, and extra spaces are ignored.

What happens to my data if I delete the plugin?

Deleting the plugin removes its scan results and settings from the database.

Does it cost anything?

The plugin is free and licensed under GPL-2.0-or-later, and nothing in it is limited or locked. A separate paid add-on, Mashlink Pro – Add-on, adds bulk fixing of orphan pages and is sold on mashlinkwp.com.

Can developers extend or unhook it?

Yes. The main class is not final and its methods are public or protected, so it can be extended. Every hook is registered with the shared instance, so it can be removed or re-prioritised, for example: remove_action( 'save_post', array( WPMash_Link_Auditor::instance(), 'on_save' ), 20 );. The wpmash_ila_loaded action passes the instance once the plugin is ready. Filters: wpmash_ila_post_types, wpmash_ila_anchor_limit, wpmash_ila_anchor_share, wpmash_ila_scan_custom_fields, wpmash_ila_opp_limit, wpmash_ila_opp_match, wpmash_ila_synonyms, wpmash_ila_keyphrases, wpmash_ila_use_seo_keyphrases, wpmash_ila_skip_own_topic, wpmash_ila_use_locations, wpmash_ila_not_locations, wpmash_ila_regions (region name => list of places), wpmash_ila_weak_words, wpmash_ila_anchor_cap, wpmash_ila_use_taxonomy_scope. Add-ons can use the wpmash_ila_fix_available filter and the wpmash_ila_render_fix action for the Fix links tab, the wpmash_ila_related_available filter and the wpmash_ila_render_related action for the Related words tab, and the wpmash_ila_map_available filter and the wpmash_ila_render_map action for the Topical Clusters tab.
sections.changelog:
1.9.5

  • New: extra tabs from the Pro add-on (Report, AI access) appear in the dashboard through the wpmash_ila_pro_tabs filter and the wpmash_ila_render_tab_<slug> action.
  • Tweak: the Link Opportunities tab shows a built-in example of the editor panel in place of a screenshot, and the unused screenshot file is removed.
  • Tweak: the readme lists the Pro features and the compatibility details as bullets.
  • Tweak: page builder detection covers Elementor, Bricks and Breakdance.
  • Fix: code-quality fixes from the Plugin Check report (sanitised input, no suppress_filters, Stable tag matches the version).

1.9.4

  • Tested with WordPress 7.1.5 and PHP 8.4.
  • New: Link suggestions now follow location and taxonomies by selection.
  • New: Location awareness. A page about one place (for example “in Miami”) is no longer offered a link to a page about another place (for example “in Vancouver”). Pages about the same place are suggested first. You can set the place yourself with the “This is a location-based topic” checkbox and Location field in the editor panel.
  • New: A link to the page’s own parent page is ranked higher in the suggestions.
  • New: Weak words such as “best”, “guide”, “services” or “event” no longer make a suggestion on their own.
  • New: The same anchor text is not suggested for the same page more than five times. The wpmash_ila_anchor_cap filter changes the number.
  • New: A “Primary keyword” field in the Internal Linking Opportunities panel of the editor. The keyword a page should rank for is never suggested as a link anchor to another page. Without a keyword, the plugin uses the focus keyphrase from Yoast SEO, Rank Math, SEOPress or All in One SEO, and then the main subject of the page title. The wpmash_ila_skip_own_topic filter turns this off.
  • Tweak: Each suggestion shows a small “Same location” or “Same region” note when it applies.
  • New: A “Link Opportunities” tab with a short guide and screenshot that shows how to find link opportunities in the block editor.
  • New: Each link in the Incoming links and Outgoing links lists has two actions, Edit link and Remove link. Edit link opens the page in the block editor, scrolls to the link and highlights it.
  • New: The lists show one row per link, and the headings name the page: “Pages that linked to [page]” and “[page] linked to”.
  • New: A Pro tab for the Pro version.
  • Changed: The Content tab is now Content & Links, with the columns Title, Incoming links, Outgoing links, Depth, Type and Status. The anchor text column is gone; anchor texts are on the Anchors tab.
  • Changed: The box for your own related words moves into the Related words tab of the Pro add-on. The built-in list stays free, and any list you saved earlier keeps working.
  • Tweak: Improved editor panel UI.
  • Tweak: A cleaner dashboard: a slimmer header, flat tabs with icons, a table with light borders, light blue number links and soft status labels.
  • Tweak: Removed unused code and styles.
  • Developers: the wpmash_ila_fix_available filter and wpmash_ila_render_fix action let an add-on provide the Bulk Fix Links tab. The wpmash_ila_related_available filter and wpmash_ila_render_related action provide the Related words tab, and wpmash_ila_map_available with wpmash_ila_render_map provide the Topical Clusters tab.

1.9.3

  • New: Link opportunities also match the page title, so pages whose title is printed by a template (hero sections, dynamic title tags) are found.
  • New: Grammar words and generic title words are ignored when finding a match, and the rarest words of a title count most. The suggested anchor keeps the natural wording of your text, for example “WordPress SEO for Isak”.
  • New: The main subject of a title counts on its own. A page titled “Rebuilding a Luxury Travel Website From a Bloated Page Builder” is suggested for the text “luxury travel website”.
  • New: A page with a one-word address such as /seo/ can be suggested when the text also contains another word of its title (“seo services”). The single word alone is not enough.
  • Developers: new filter wpmash_ila_generic_words.

1.9.2

  • New: Semantic matching for link opportunities. Related words such as “cost” and “price” count as the same meaning. Uses a short built-in list plus your own related words, added in the Diagnose box.
  • New: Link opportunities also use the focus keyphrases saved by Yoast SEO, Rank Math, SEOPress and All in One SEO, and the SEO title saved by Slim SEO.
  • New: Overall Link Health now sits in the page header with a progress ring. The issue summary shows as a line of links under the scan button.
  • New: Red attention dots on the tabs that need attention after a scan.
  • New: The pop-ups behind the In, Out and anchor numbers show a table with the page, the anchor text and a Remove link action.
  • New: Plugin icon, header logo, table header colour and a dark blue Run full scan button.
  • Cleaner message when no broken or redirected links are found.
  • Developers: new filters wpmash_ila_synonyms, wpmash_ila_keyphrases and wpmash_ila_use_seo_keyphrases.

1.9.1

  • New: Overall Link Health score and a summary of issues on the dashboard after a scan.
  • New: Depth column showing the clicks from the homepage.
  • The Ignore button now shows only for flagged anchors.

1.9.0

  • New: Internal Linking Opportunities in the block editor. Find link opportunities with Mashlink and insert a link in one click. Works with ACF fields and ACF blocks.
  • New: Remove link button in the report pop-ups.
  • New: “Scan completed” pop-up and a “Scan first” notice.
  • New: Stop scan and Stop check buttons while a scan or link check is running.
  • Developers: the class can be extended and its hooks removed with WPMash_Link_Auditor::instance().
  • New header and icon, and lighter status blocks.

1.7.9

  • Overused anchors are now judged per page: the same anchor must be used more than 4 times for one page and be over 15% of that page’s links. Big sites no longer get flags just for reaching 5 uses.
  • Added a Settings link on the Plugins screen.
  • Added a “View details” link on the Plugins screen that opens the WordPress.org plugin information pop-up.
  • The admin page and menu are now called Mashlink.
  • Image-only and empty links are no longer listed; only links with readable anchor text are audited.
  • Only links inside the body text are counted. Previous/next post links, pagination, categories, tags, author and meta links, breadcrumbs, related-post lists, sidebars and other layout areas are ignored.
  • Button links (theme buttons, WordPress and GenerateBlocks buttons, builder buttons) are left out by default. A new “Include button links” checkbox adds them.
  • Added a “How we measure overuse” tooltip on the report.
  • The Content tab now lists the most linked-to pages first, with a blue “Top Linked Page” badge on the single most linked page. Click the Status column to sort by status instead.
  • The red overused-anchor box was removed from the Content tab; overused anchors are shown on the Anchor texts tab.
  • Added a note that Deep scan is slower and can be skipped.
  • Dynamic-tag placeholders in saved content (for example {{post_permalink}}) are no longer listed as links.
  • Re-run the full scan after updating to rebuild the report.

1.7.7

  • The link checker no longer requests other websites. A redirect that leaves the site is reported with its destination and is not followed.

1.7.6

  • Author and company set to WPmash (wpmash.com).

1.7.5

  • Renamed to Mashlink.

1.7.4

  • Renamed.

1.7.3

  • Renamed.

1.7.2

  • Tested with WordPress 7.1.
  • Renamed to Mashlink.
  • Code standard fixes: translator comments, input sanitizing, removed set_time_limit and suppress_filters.

1.7.1

  • Links stored in custom fields (ACF and similar) are now scanned.

1.7.0

  • Added the Diagnose box.

1.6.0

  • Added CSV export.

1.5.0

  • Added the Broken & redirected links tab.

1.4.0

  • Deep scan works with any theme or builder. Added search.
